newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia government hopeful on jobs bill approval.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia government hopeful on jobs bill approval.

text.p: The Australian government is hopeful its controversial labour reform bill will pass the upper house Senate on Tuesday afternoon, a spokesman for government Senate leader Robert Hill said on Tuesday.
"We're still hopeful of getting it through today," the spokesman told Reuters. "Obviously we want to get it finished and there's no reason why it shouldn't be."
He said debate on the bill had taken 44 hours and 35 minutes so far, compared with an initial estimate of 25 hours.
"We've almost doubled that and it's now the second longest debate on a bill in the Senate," the spokesman said.

On Monday, the spokesman said the Workplace Relations Bill was likely to pass the final stage in the parliamentary process before midnight (1300 GMT) on that day, but an amendment proposed by the Greens dragged out the debate.
Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith struck a deal with the Democrats in late October, in which the minor party would support the bill as long as 171 amendments were made.
The government needs two non-government votes to pass any legislation in the Senate.
Reforms contained in the bill will deregulate the labour market and will give unions a weaker role in wage negotiations.
The changes are expected to take effect by February next year.
